deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck defines an 'analyseur' Ω. It is a commutative pseudo-ring (a ring that need not have a unit), with sum x+y and product xy. It carries a second law (F,G) ↦ F∘G that is associative and has a two-sided identity, written Ξ, I or T. The page first says 'loi de composition unitaire' and replaces it with 'loi de monoïde'.

Axiom 2: for each G, right composition F ↦ F∘G is a pseudo-ring homomorphism, so (F+F')∘G = F∘G + F'∘G and (FF')∘G = (F∘G)(F'∘G). Axioms 1–2 are exactly a 'composition ring' (Menger–Adler tri-operational algebra) without commutativity of ∘.

Axiom 3 ('fonctorialité') is the new ingredient. For every F there are finitely many pairs (F'_i, F''_i) with F∘(G'+G'') = Σ (F'_i∘G')(F''_i∘G'') for all G', G''. Similarly there are pairs (Φ'_α, Φ''_α) with F∘(G'G'') = Σ (Φ'_α∘G')(Φ''_α∘G''). So every element has a finite 'addition formula' and 'multiplication formula'. Read as a co-addition Δ+F = Σ F'_i⊗F''_i and a co-multiplication Δ×F = Σ Φ'_α⊗Φ''_α, this is precisely the structure of a plethory (Tall–Wraith 1970; Borger–Wieland 2005), stated elementwise as existence conditions. It is also a finiteness condition of 'representative function' type, as with polynomials, numerical polynomials, or symmetric functions under plethysm.

Grothendieck then studies constants. Since 0∘G = 0 by axiom 2, (F∘0)∘G = F∘(0∘G) = F∘0, so F∘0 is a constant: λ is constant if λ∘F = λ for all F. The constants Ω_0 form a sub-pseudo-ring, and it is stable under ∘ because λ∘μ = λ. For λ ∈ Ω_0, F∘λ is again constant, so Ω acts on Ω_0 by F(λ) := F∘λ, i.e. elements of Ω are 'functions' on the ring of constants. Setting Ω^0 = {F : F(0) = 0}, one gets Ω = Ω_0 ⊕ Ω^0 via F = F(0) + (F − F(0)).

A unital analyseur has a multiplicative unit 1 that is a constant (1∘F = 1). Then Ω_0 is a unital ring with the same unit. The aim seems to be an abstract algebraic theory of 'rings of operations/functions closed under composition', with the action Ω × Ω_0 → Ω_0 as the evaluation map.
errors: Axiom 3a is problematic in the non-unital case. Take F = T (the ∘-identity) and G'' = 0. Then G' = Σ (F'_i∘G')·(F''_i(0)), so every G' must lie in the ideal Ω·Ω_0 generated by constants. Example: xZ[x] under composition has Ω_0 = 0, so 3a fails for T. A correct non-unital version must allow linear terms (F'_j∘G' + F''_k∘G'' + Σ products), i.e. a co-addition into the augmented tensor product. In the unital case this issue disappears because one may take F'' = 1.

The decomposition F'_i, F''_i is only asserted to exist, not as a structure (no tensor product, no coassociativity or counit axioms). That suffices for the 'functorial' intent but is weaker than a plethory unless Ω acts faithfully.
In the unital definition, 1∘F = 1 is a genuine extra axiom: axiom 2 only makes 1∘G an idempotent. The page correctly imposes it.
Minor slips: 3a writes G'_i for G'. In 3b the sum is indexed by i but the family by α.

ideas.what: Commutative pseudo-ring with an associative unital composition law, right-distributive and right-multiplicative
ideas.usually_credited_to: K. Menger (1940s), I. Adler 'Composition rings' (Duke Math J. 1962)

ideas.what: Finite addition and multiplication formulas F∘(G'+G'') = Σ(F'_i∘G')(F''_i∘G''), F∘(G'G'') = Σ(Φ'_α∘G')(Φ''_α∘G'')
ideas.modern_name: plethory (biring with composition; Tall–Wraith monoid), co-addition and co-multiplication of a biring
ideas.usually_credited_to: D. Tall & G. Wraith (1970); J. Borger & B. Wieland 'Plethystic algebra' (2005); Bergman–Hausknecht (1996)
ideas.where_published: unsure (λ-rings, a prototype, come from Grothendieck's 1957 Riemann–Roch work, but this axiomatics is not in published texts as far as I know)

ideas.what: Constants (λ∘F = λ), the subring Ω_0, the action of Ω on Ω_0 by evaluation F(λ) = F∘λ, and the splitting Ω = Ω_0 ⊕ Ω^0 by F(0)
ideas.modern_name: constant/augmentation splitting; evaluation action of a plethory on its ring of constants (P acting on the coefficient ring)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in composition-ring and plethory literature

missed.claim: Around April 1982 (printout dated 82.109), Grothendieck formulates, under the name 'analyseur', an elementwise version of what is now called a plethory. It is a composition ring whose elements have finite co-addition and co-multiplication formulas. This predates Borger–Wieland's 'Plethystic algebra' (2005) and links his λ-ring legacy to the later plethory/Witt-vector programme (Borger's 'geometry over F_1'). This early independent formulation by Grothendieck seems not to be recorded in the literature.
missed.quote: 3) (Fonctorialité) a) ∀F∈Ω, ∃ famille finie (F_i', F_i''), ... telle que F∘(G'+G'') = Σ_i (F_i'∘G')(F_i''∘G'')
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historians of plethories and λ-rings (Tall–Wraith → Borger–Wieland → Borger's F_1 geometry) could add Grothendieck's 1982 'analyseurs' as an independent precursor. The pages may show what motivated him (the name suggests 'analysis' operators acting on a ring of constants).

missed.claim: The theory breaks off right after the definitions of constants and unital analyseurs. Questions left open include examples, a classification, free analyseurs, and the relation to λ-rings and to rings of 'functions' on Ω_0.
missed.quote: Ainsi, Ω "opère" sur Ω_0 par (F,λ) ↦ F(λ) := F∘λ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a natural entry point. When is Ω determined by its action on Ω_0-algebras (i.e. a plethory represented as operations)? The question is studied today only in the plethory framework.

deep.surprise_reason: These are clean but elementary definitions. The notable point is that Grothendieck, in 1982, independently axiomatizes plethory-like 'composition rings with finite addition/multiplication formulas', a notion later central in Borger–Wieland. I am not aware of this being recorded. Axiom 3a also has a flaw in the non-unital case.
transcription_corrections: In axiom 3a, 'G_i'' should read G' (no index): F∘(G'+G'') = Σ_i (F_i'∘G')(F_i''∘G'').
In axiom 3b the family is indexed by α: Σ_α (Φ'_α∘G')(Φ''_α∘G'').
Second line of the definition originally read 'loi de composition unitaire (pas nécess. commun.)', crossed out and replaced by 'loi de monoïde'. 'y et sa loi additive' is crossed out.
In the stability remark: 'car λ∘μ = λ pour λ, μ ∈ Ω_0' (μ may be taken in Ω).
Last lines read: 'Donc Ω_0 est alors un anneau unitaire, admettant même unité que Ω'.
The fragment '[Ne dépend que de la structure F∘G] pas +' likely means the notion of constant depends only on ∘, not on +.
